name: Produce a binaural-beat meditation track: a two-chord pad foundation with long reverb and overlapping glided notes, a sparse echoing piano and subtle bass, volume-automated arrangement, then a binaural layer of two pure sines (440 Hz and 432 Hz for an 8 Hz difference) panned hard left/right, a narrow high-Q EQ cut at the carrier frequency on the music bus so nothing masks it, fades, a gentle limiter (~3 dB input, no audible gain reduction) and WAV/MP3 export at 44.1 kHz
goal: Make the whole track, not just the beat. Start from pads: play a simple two-chord loop (around A and D), add reverb with high decay and wet mix, keep chord changes on the grid, and let notes overlap with glide so transitions slide instead of stepping. Add a short piano line with an echo (more feedback, ping-pong on) and its own reverb, then a subtle low bass on the same roots; pull all levels down to avoid overdrive. Arrange by drawing volume automation so elements enter and leave (less is more; one element can carry minutes), boost the highs with a high shelf on bright parts, put delay before reverb. Binaural layer: a sine at the root frequency (A = 440 Hz) and a duplicate at 432 Hz (8 Hz difference); unpanned they make an audible wobble (monaural beat), panned hard left and right they form the binaural beat. Group the music and cut a narrow notch (high Q) at 440 Hz so the instrumental doesn't overlap the carrier. Fade the beat in and out, keep it quiet but present when muted/unmuted. On the master, add a limiter on the loudest section with only ~3 dB input and no audible gain reduction; export 44.1 kHz WAV plus an MP3, then do a calm test listen later and adjust.

source.title: Producing a Binaural Beats Meditation Track in Ableton Live (Step-By-Step)
source.transcript_note: Long DAW walkthrough; coaching/one-on-one call promo and project-download talk dropped; numeric values are the presenter's.

prerequisites: DAW with stock pad/piano/bass instruments, reverb, echo/delay, EQ, utility gain and limiter, or Web Audio: two OscillatorNodes (f and f-Δ) each through a StereoPannerNode at -1/+1, a BiquadFilter type 'notch' at f with high Q on the music bus, a DynamicsCompressor as gentle limiter (implementation note)
Headphones for checking the binaural layer

inputs.name: root_hz
inputs.description: Carrier frequency matching the track's root (440 Hz for A in the video)

inputs.name: beat_hz
inputs.description: Left/right difference (8 Hz in the video)

inputs.name: chords
inputs.description: Simple pad progression (A and D in the video)

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
No health or brainwave-entrainment claims are made by this skill; it is a sound-construction recipe only. Keep pulse/beat layers at low listening level.
Without hard left/right panning the two sines only produce a monaural wobble.
Skip the notch and other instruments around the carrier frequency mask it; cut narrowly so the music isn't thinned.
Avoid heavy compression/limiting in meditation music; no audible distortion or pumping.
Factory preset names are not needed; any soft pad, piano and bass work. Bit depth depends on the distributor.

steps.action: Pick a soft pad, play a simple two-chord loop (e.g. A then D), add reverb with high decay and wet mix, capture the MIDI and align chord changes to the grid; loop it.
Layer a second pad for texture and a sparse piano phrase; add an echo with more feedback and ping-pong, plus a reverb with moderated wet mix.
steps.expect: A moving echo line over the pads

steps.action: Lengthen notes so they overlap at chord changes and enable glide so pitch slides between them.
steps.expect: Smooth gliding transitions instead of steps

steps.action: Add a subtle low bass on the roots; lower all instrument levels to avoid clipping.
Arrange with volume automation: bring elements in and out gradually; high-shelf boost and mid cut on bright parts; put delay before reverb.
steps.expect: A slowly evolving track that starts and ends gently

steps.action: Binaural layer: a sine instrument at 440 Hz and a duplicate at 432 Hz; listen unpanned (wobble), then pan one hard left and one hard right; program one note across the whole track.
steps.expect: Two pure tones forming an 8 Hz binaural beat on headphones

steps.action: Group the music tracks and add a narrow, high-Q EQ cut at 440 Hz on the group.
steps.expect: The beat sounds clean, without resonance from the music

steps.action: Fade the beat in and out; set its level so it is quiet but noticeably different when muted.
On the master, loop the loudest section and add a limiter with about 3 dB input and no audible gain reduction; export WAV 44.1 kHz and an MP3; test-listen later in a calm setting and adjust.

verification: Left channel contains only the 440 Hz sine and right only the 432 Hz sine (check by soloing each side).
A spectrum of the music group shows a narrow dip at 440 Hz.
The limiter shows little or no gain reduction on the loudest section.
